findings.title: Mixed cleanup outcomes cannot persist terminal ROLLBACK_FAILED
findings.observation: persistRollbackCleanupEvidence derives one aggregate/reference status from all three branches. When valid terminal restore cleanup is FAIL but independently authorized production cleanup is PASS, the shared reference status is FAIL. executeRollbackWithCleanup passes that FAIL reference to completeLifecycle for production, which tries to build state CLEANED; verifyLifecycle requires CLEANED references to have status PASS and throws RESOURCE_LIFECYCLE_REFERENCE_STATE.
findings.trigger: Start actual rollback from an exact valid terminal RESTORE CLEANUP_FAILED forward record on a fresh target, return application rollback NOT_APPLICABLE, and allow production cleanup to prove zero application rows and delete its exact attempt-owned resources successfully.
findings.impact: Production resources are deleted and rollback-cleanup.json is durably written with status FAIL, but production-lifecycle.json remains QUIESCING and terminal-rollback-evidence.json is absent. Retry then observes an empty live project against a nonempty frozen production set and conflicts with the immutable aggregate, so the attempt cannot reach the required durable ROLLBACK_FAILED state.

evidence.description: A temporary exact-head Vitest regression created valid forward CLEANUP_FAILED authority, ran actual rollback, and reproduced RESOURCE_LIFECYCLE_REFERENCE_STATE after one application rollback call, all three production deletes, and FAIL aggregate persistence; no terminal evidence existed and production remained QUIESCING. The temporary test was removed and the worktree returned clean.
A fresh-context independent reviewer traced the same aggregate-status/per-scope-state mismatch and confirmed it prevents durable ROLLBACK_FAILED terminalization.
The aggregate reference status becomes FAIL when any branch fails, while both scope lifecycles receive that same reference even when production result is PASS.
The new matrix first creates valid CLEANUP_FAILED authority but then always corrupts it; no committed test leaves that valid evidence unchanged and exercises the mixed result.

The design failure matrix allows independently authorized production cleanup when restore cleanup fails and requires the aggregate/attempt to end failed, while lifecycle invariants require CLEANED to bind PASS and CLEANUP_FAILED to bind FAIL.

findings.remediation: Represent or reference per-scope cleanup outcomes so a successful production lifecycle can bind a PASS production result while the restore lifecycle retains its FAIL forward authority and the aggregate/terminal result remains FAIL. Do not weaken CLEANED=PASS or CLEANUP_FAILED=FAIL lifecycle invariants. Ensure the aggregate and terminal envelope still resolve both exact scope results without circular or conflicting authority.
findings.verification: Add an actual-rollback regression that leaves valid terminal CLEANUP_FAILED forward evidence unchanged and requires application NOT_APPLICABLE, production PASS/CLEANED, restore FAIL/CLEANUP_FAILED, aggregate FAIL, terminal ROLLBACK_FAILED, and replay without a second delete or aggregate conflict. Also cover the symmetric mixed-result shape if it is reachable.
